title: Bump myst-parser from 5.1.0 to 5.2.0
body:
Bumps [myst-parser](https://github.com/executablebooks/MyST-Parser) from 5.1.0 to 5.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from myst-parser's releases.

v5.2.0

Heading anchors are now stable and documented: one shared slug implementation with "github", "gitlab" and "docutils" presets, slugs emitted as real HTML ids, explicit (target)= ids taking priority, and a versioned anchor contract. Warnings and other tools now get accurate source lines (also inside {include}d files), docutils 0.23 is supported, inputs that used to abort the build now warn instead, and many fixes land for references, images, front matter, substitutions and directives; a new section_ref extension links §1.1-style references to numbered headings.

Nothing is dropped: Python >=3.11, Sphinx >=8,<10 and the markdown-it-py requirement are unchanged, mdit-py-plugins is raised to ~=0.7 (it was ~=0.6,>=0.6.1), and the docutils range is widened to >=0.20,<0.24. Some of these changes can still alter the output of a project that built before, so please read the upgrade notes.

‼️ Upgrade notes

  • Heading anchors (#1158, #1168), see docs:
    • Duplicate heading slugs now get fixed-base suffixes, x, x-1, x-2, as on GitHub; the third and later duplicates used to get x-1-2, x-1-2-3, ... So a link that uses the old slug of a third or later duplicate, such as [](https://github.com/executablebooks/MyST-Parser/blob/HEAD/#x-1-2), no longer resolves and warns (myst.xref_missing, which fails a -W build): change it to [](https://github.com/executablebooks/MyST-Parser/blob/HEAD/#x-2). Links to the first two duplicates are unchanged, and every HTML id a heading had before is kept.
    • Slugs are also emitted as secondary HTML ids on the rendered headings, so #slug links work in the published HTML. The docutils id stays the primary (first) id, so existing fragment links keep working. Set myst_heading_anchors_html_ids = False to emit only the docutils id.
    • An explicit (target)= placed before a heading becomes the section's primary id, which tocs, permalinks and objects.inv use; the implicit heading id is kept as a secondary anchor.
    • A heading whose slug is empty (a punctuation-only title, or any non-Latin title with the "docutils" preset) gets no anchor, and an empty fragment, [](https://github.com/executablebooks/MyST-Parser/blob/HEAD/#), now warns as unresolved.
    • Links that used to warn now resolve when the anchor exists: same-document links to implicit ids (such as headings deeper than myst_heading_anchors; under Sphinx only as a last resort), and cross-document links to label ids and to the implicit ids of headings within the myst_heading_anchors depth. [](https://github.com/executablebooks/MyST-Parser/blob/HEAD/doc.md#label) takes the target's title as its text (#1207).
    • These rules (slug presets, deduplication, empty slugs, explicit-id priority and HTML ids) are now a documented contract, pinned by a versioned, language-agnostic corpus (tests/fixtures/slugs.json). myst_parser.mdit_to_docutils.base.default_slugify is deprecated in favour of myst_parser.slugs.github_slugify.
  • Directive option warnings (#1164): each warning now points at the offending option's line, and unknown options are reported one per warning, as Unknown option key: 'x' (allowed: [...]), instead of one aggregate Unknown option keys: [...]. The myst.directive_option subtype is unchanged, so suppress_warnings keeps working, but tests that match the old message need updating.
  • Directive API (#1164): directives now receive the full fenced text as block_text, as in reStructuredText, so errors that echo it show the whole fence; and content_offset is -1 when the body starts on the opening line.
  • Source lines (#1164, #1169, #1179): lines in warnings and nodes change where they were wrong. Text nodes no longer take the line of the most recent directive (so gettext .pot locations change), lines inside {include}d files are no longer one late, and the body of a directive with options and a trailing blank line is no longer one line off.
  • Front matter (#1197): options that can only be set globally (heading_slug_func, update_mathjax, mathjax_classes, suppress_warnings, inventories)

... (truncated)

Sourced from myst-parser's changelog.

title: fix: keep optional parens when two type: ignore comments would share a line
body:
## Summary

A parenthesized right-hand side whose last body line and closing bracket each carry a
`# type: ignore` comment is unstable: dropping the optional parens puts both comments on
one physical line, Python only reads the first one, and Black's equivalence check then
sees a missing `TypeIgnore` node:

```
error: cannot format example.py: INTERNAL ERROR: Black 0.1.dev50+gb4f1fcae4 on Python
(CPython) 3.14.9 produced code that is not equivalent to the source.
```

`can_omit_invisible_parens` already keeps the parens for the "type ignore plus another
comment" combination and for multiple type ignores in the same line, but not for one
type ignore in the body and one after the closing bracket. This adds that case.

## Reproduction

```python
x = (
    f(a)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
)  # type: ignore[assignment]
```

Before: `INTERNAL ERROR`, the file is left unformatted.
After: left unchanged.

## Changes

- `src/black/lines.py`: in `can_omit_invisible_parens`, return `False` when both
  `rhs.body` and `rhs.tail` carry a `# type: ignore` comment.
- `tests/data/cases/type_ignore_comment_closing_paren.py`: the reproduction as an
  idempotent case.
- `CHANGES.md`: entry under "Stable style".

## Tests

- `pytest tests/test_format.py -q` → 315 passed (includes the new case).
- `pytest tests/test_black.py -q` → 213 passed, 11 skipped; the two
  `*_with_color` failures also fail on `main` on this Windows machine and are unrelated.

Fixes #5684

title: Fix crash when removing parentheses would merge two type-ignore comments
body:
### Description

Fixes #5684. Closes #5685, closes #5688

Alternative fix to #5685, prepared independently before that PR was found.

Keep the outer parentheses when the last expression inside them and the closing
parenthesis each have a `# type: ignore` comment. Removing them previously put both
comments on one line, lost a type-ignore node and failed the AST safety check.

The regression fixture covers calls, collections, subscripts, attributes, nested
expressions and the reported PyTorch example. Ordinary-comment controls keep their
existing formatting.

The new fixture fails with the base function and passes with the fix. The full
suite reports 650 passed, 12 skipped and two color-output failures that reproduce
on the clean base. Notebook tests: 102 passed. Self-format and all changed-file
pre-commit hooks pass. Full-repository mypy has one unchanged Windows unreachable
statement error, also reproduced on base.

title: Fix INTERNAL ERROR when paren removal joins two `# type: ignore` comments
body:
### Description

Fixes #5684.

When a line inside redundant parentheses and the line after them each carry a `# type: ignore` comment, removing the parentheses joins both comments onto one line. Only the first `# type: ignore` on a line applies, so the second one is silently lost, the formatted file no longer has an equivalent AST, and Black crashes with an INTERNAL ERROR.

`maybe_make_parens_invisible_in_atom` already keeps the parentheses when their own prefixes carry a `# type: ignore`, but it never looked at the prefix of the leaf following the closing parenthesis. This adds that check (with a small `_following_leaf` helper mirroring `preceding_leaf`), so the parentheses stay visible in exactly this case.

Since this fixes a crash rather than changing the style, it is not gated behind `--preview`, like the earlier INTERNAL ERROR fixes #5618 and #5625.

title: Format each notebook cell once when it is already formatted
body:
### Description

`format_cell()` passes the cell source to `format_str()` without a trailing newline. The first formatting pass always adds one, so every cell counts as changed: it gets the forced second pass, then `check_stability_and_equivalence()` runs `assert_equivalent()` and a third pass in `assert_stable()`. On an already formatted notebook, which is the usual `--check` and pre-commit case, each cell is formatted three times plus an AST comparison, only for the result to be discarded with `NothingChanged`.

This change appends the newline before formatting (the result is still stripped of trailing newlines afterwards, as before) and skips the safe mode checks when the formatted cell is identical to its input. That's the rule `format_file_contents()` already follows for `.py` files, which raise `NothingChanged` before checking. Cells that do change are checked exactly as before.

Measured with `format_file_contents(src, fast=False, mode=Mode(is_ipynb=True))`, upstream and patched `format_cell()` swapped in the same process, alternating order, CPython 3.14 without mypyc (median CPU time, 5 rounds):

| notebook | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| MuJoCo tutorial, already formatted | 1112 ms | 390 ms | 2.85x |
| Qualtran Ising example, already formatted | 1671 ms | 573 ms | 2.92x |
| 3-cell notebook, already formatted | 2.3 ms | 1.4 ms | 1.69x |
| MuJoCo tutorial, needs reformatting | 1138 ms | 1069 ms | 1.06x |

A differential run over 660 cells (test case sources with IPython magics, cell magics, trailing semicolons, trailing comments, backslashes, CRLF line endings, empty and whitespace-only cells, with and without `--fast`) and the notebooks above gave identical output and identical errors before and after.

title: Fix crash on backslash-only lines in code Black leaves as is
body:
### Description

a line that's only a backslash, right after another backslash continuation, makes Black crash on code it's supposed to leave alone:

```python
# fmt: off
x = [1,
     2] + \
    \
    [3]
# fmt: on
```

that gives `INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced invalid code`. same thing on a `# fmt: skip` line and on lines outside `--line-ranges`. in an f-string field with `=`, or any t-string field, the field's source is part of the string, so it's "not equivalent to the source" instead, and with `--fast` Black just writes the changed string. CPython's own `Lib/test/test_tstring.py` hits it. it's a regression from 24.8.0, 24.4.2 handles all of these.

since #4343, `transform_whitespace` only turns the first backslash-newline into an NL token. the second one gets skipped, so the driver puts a plain newline in the prefix where the backslash was. regular code gets its whitespace redone so it doesn't matter there, but fmt: off/skip code and f-string fields are written straight from the prefix. now a backslash line that follows a backslash NL becomes an NL token too, so it stays in the prefix. `list_comments` still counts it as an empty line, so comments land where they did before.

output only changes where Black used to crash or drop the backslash, so already formatted files come out the same.

a lone backslash right after a regular newline still turns into a blank line, same as before. handling that too would also fix `f"""{value` / `\` / `=}"""`, but it changes blank lines after comments, so I left it out.

title: Skip the quote regexes when a string body has nothing to escape
body:
### Description

`normalize_string_quotes` compiles and runs three regular expressions for each string. When the string body has no backslash and no character of the new quote, these expressions change nothing. This change returns early in that case. The output does not change.

| Benchmark | 3.11 | 3.14 | 3.14 mypyc |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `normalize_string_quotes`, 8 simple strings | -90% | -88% | -93% |
| `normalize_string_quotes`, 12 strings with escapes | -0.5% | +0.4% | -1.7% |
| `format_str`, 300 lines of double-quoted strings | -8.0% | -6.9% | -4.1% |
| `format_str`, `profiling/mix_small.py` | +0.2% | 0% | -2.6% |

The changes for strings with escapes and for `mix_small.py` are not significant. With mypyc, the noise was up to 3%, so only the `normalize_string_quotes` result is significant there. I measured no slowdown on strings that need escapes, raw strings, f-strings, or the other 19 benchmarks. I used 20 to 40 interleaved rounds and a Mann-Whitney test (Apple M5). I did not measure other architectures.

Checks:
- `pytest` passes, and `black --check`, `flake8`, and `isort` are clean.
- Old and new `normalize_string_quotes` gave the same result on 1,000,000 random string literals.
- Old and new `format_str` output matched on 12,968 inputs in 8 modes (`tests/data`, the standard library, and random line slices).

title: Fix unstable formatting of a comment-only fmt: off/on block before a tuple assignment
body:
### Description

A comment-only `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on` block right before an assignment whose target is a tuple makes Black fail its stability check:

```console
$ printf 'x = 1\n# fmt: off\n# fmt: on\na, b = c\n' | black -
error: cannot format -: INTERNAL ERROR: Black ... produced different code on the second pass of the formatter.
```

Each pass adds blank lines before `# fmt: off`. The same happens for `(a, b) = c`, `a, = c` and `*a, b = c`.

`_handle_comment_only_fmt_block` inserts the STANDALONE_COMMENT next to the leaf that carried the comments in its prefix. For `a, b = c` that leaf is `a`, inside the `testlist_star_expr` of the target. The target is then wrapped in invisible parentheses, so the comment line starts with an invisible `(` and renders as an extra empty line on every pass.

When the leaf starts the target of an assignment, the comment is now inserted before the whole target instead, in the `expr_stmt`. That is where it already goes for a plain `a = c`, which formats fine. Other statements keep the current behavior.

### Checklist - did you ...

- [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary?
- [x] Add / update tests if necessary?

title: Fix async statements dropped after a comment-only fmt: off/on block
body:
### Description

A `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on` pair with nothing but comments between them, placed right before an `async def`, `async for` or `async with`, makes Black lose the statement:

```console
$ printf 'x = 1\n# fmt: off\n# fmt: on\nasync def f():\n    pass\n' | black --fast -q -
x = 1
# fmt: off
# fmt: on
```

Without `--fast` it fails with "produced code that is not equivalent to the source" instead.

The comment-only block becomes a STANDALONE_COMMENT in front of `async` inside the `async_stmt` node. `visit_async_stmt` stopped at the first STANDALONE_COMMENT (that check is there for `# fmt: skip` on the header, where `async` itself becomes the comment) and then visited only the next child, which was `async`. The `def`/`for`/`with` node was never visited.

The loop plus `next()` was left over from when the inner statement was visited differently in preview. Visiting the children in order does the same thing for the normal and `# fmt: skip` cases and also covers this one. It also fixes a comment-only block followed by an `async def` header with `# fmt: skip`, which produced invalid code.

title: Document configuration lookup with --stdin-filename
body:
### Description

The configuration docs say stdin lookup starts from the working directory. With

title: Fix crash on `# fmt: skip` on several one-line clauses of a statement
body:
### Description

`# fmt: skip` on two one-line clauses of the same statement crashes when their bodies are separated by semicolons:

```python
if x: f(); g()  # fmt: skip
else: f(); g()  # fmt: skip
```

```console
$ black example.py
error: cannot format example.py: INTERNAL ERROR: Black 26.10.2.dev98+gb4f1fcae4 on Python (CPython) 3.13.12 produced different code on the second pass of the formatter.
```

The same happens with `elif`, `try`/`except`/`finally` and `for`/`while`/`async for` with `else`, whenever a skipped one-line clause follows another skipped one-line clause. 26.10.1 formats this example; bisecting points to #5633. With bare names as the bodies (`if x: a; b  # fmt: skip` / `else: a; b  # fmt: skip`) it also crashes on 26.10.1.

For a one-line clause, `_get_compound_statement_header` prepends the clause's header to the skipped nodes (#4800). It collects every child of the compound statement before the body, so for the `else` line it starts at `if`. By then the `if` line has been hidden by its own `# fmt: skip`: the statement holds a `STANDALONE_COMMENT` and the `simple_stmt` with the newline left of its body. Both were hidden a second time with the `else` line, and since #5633 a newline is added after hidden code whose last line holds a comment, so the newline came out twice and blank lines were added before `else` on every pass. This starts the header after an already hidden clause and what is left of its body (a `suite` or `simple_stmt` with no code), so `else` only takes `else:`.

The new case is `fmtskip_one_liner_later_clause.py`; it fails on `main`. The full test suite and the pre-commit hooks pass. Running Black over the CPython 3.13 standard library, pandas, sqlglot, ibis, haystack and Ruff's formatter fixtures (11,573 files) gives the same output and the same errors as `main`, in stable and preview.

This changes nothing for code that doesn't crash. An earlier clause that isn't skipped itself, like `if x: pass` before `else: f(); g()  # fmt: skip`, is still kept as written, as on `main` and 26.10.1, because changing that would reformat code that Black has already formatted.

This touches the same function's neighbourhood as #5674 but merges cleanly with it apart from the changelog line; the full suite passes with both.

title: Fix `# fmt: skip` on a semicolon-separated body on its own line
body:
### Description

This is the follow-up mentioned in #5588. `# fmt: skip` on a semicolon-separated body that sits on its own line joins the body to the header:

```python
if x:
    a; b  # fmt: skip
```

becomes `if x:    a; b  # fmt: skip`, and the same happens under `else:`, `except E:` and the other clauses. When two clauses in a row have such a body, Black crashes instead:

```python
if x:
    f(); g()  # fmt: skip
else:
    f(); g()  # fmt: skip
```

```console
$ black example.py
error: cannot format example.py: INTERNAL ERROR: Black 26.10.2.dev98+gb4f1fcae4 on Python (CPython) 3.13.12 produced different code on the second pass of the formatter.
```

On 26.10.1 the first example crashes ("produced invalid code"), the same block with `print(1); print(2)` as the body is joined, and `try:` / `a; b  # fmt: skip` / `except E:` / `a; b  # fmt: skip` crashes.

`_find_compound_statement_context` had two cases: a body that is a direct child of the compound statement (`if x: a; b  # fmt: skip`), and a suite with a single statement, which it took for "an expanded one-liner after Black's initial formatting pass". But the tree is the parsed source, and a skipped one-liner stays on one line, so a body in a suite was always written on its own line, and the header was prepended to the skipped nodes for it. This removes the suite case, so only that line is skipped and the header is formatted as usual. The suite branch of `_should_keep_compound_statement_inline` was only reachable from it, so it goes too.

The new case is `fmtskip_compound_body_own_line.py` (`if`/`elif`/`else`, `while`, `for`, `with`, `try`/`except`/`finally`, `class`, `def`, `async with`/`async for`, headers that need formatting); it fails on `main`. The full test suite and the pre-commit hooks pass. Running Black over the CPython 3.13 standard library, pandas, sqlglot, ibis, haystack and Ruff's formatter fixtures (11,573 files, stable and preview) gives the same output and the same errors as `main`. Code that `main` already joined (`if x:    a; b  # fmt: skip`) is left unchanged.

title: Parenthesize one-item sequence patterns in case statements
body:
### Description

Fixes #3525.

A one-item sequence pattern written without brackets, like `case "exit",:`, is left as is, while a one-element tuple elsewhere gets parentheses (`x = 1,` becomes `x = (1,)`). As suggested in https://github.com/psf/black/issues/3525#issuecomment-1404038149, this adds parentheses to such patterns under a new preview feature, `parenthesize_one_item_sequence_patterns`:

```python
# Before
match command:
    case "exit",:
        pass

# After (with --preview)
match command:
    case ("exit",):
        pass
```

`normalize_invisible_parens()` only uses visible parentheses when `is_one_tuple()` matches, and a bare pattern after `case` is a `patterns` node, which that check doesn't cover. With the feature enabled, a one-item `patterns` node now gets visible parentheses too. Patterns already in parentheses or brackets, and patterns with more than one item, are unchanged. A one-item pattern too long for the line already got parentheses when split, so that output doesn't change.

Tested with `pytest tests/test_format.py tests/test_docs.py tests/test_schema.py`, the rest of the test suite except `test_blackd.py`, and isort, flake8, mypy and prettier on the changed files.

title: Fix --line-ranges producing invalid code for stacked decorators in 2-space or tab-indented code
body:
### Description

With `--line-ranges`, lines outside the range are turned into standalone comments and reindented. Stacked decorators were merged into one standalone comment, so only the first decorator was reindented and the rest kept their old indentation. In code indented with 2 spaces or tabs that produces invalid output:

```python
class A:
  @a
  @b
  def f(self):
    pass

  def g(self):
    pass
```

```
$ black --line-ranges 7-8 dec.py
error: INTERNAL ERROR: Black 26.10.1 on Python (CPython) 3.14.7 produced invalid code:
cannot parse: dec.py:3:2
      @b
```

The first pass gives `    @a` / `  @b`. This hits "format selection" in editors on any 2-space or tab-indented file with stacked decorators. 4-space code is not affected because the old and new indentation match.

Each decorator in a `decorators` node is now converted on its own, the same way a single decorator already is, so each one gets the new indentation.

Added `tests/data/cases/line_ranges_stacked_decorators.py`; it fails before the change. `pytest tests` passes (722, excluding `test_blackd.py`, which needs the `d` extra), and flake8/mypy are clean on `ranges.py`. A line-ranges sweep over 120 real files with decorators (a range every 10 lines) gives no failures with the change; unchanged main fails on gsutil's `gslib/tests/test_gsutil.py`, which uses 2-space indentation.

title: Fix crash on a skipped async def header with a `...` body
body:
### Description Anyone who puts `# fmt: skip` on an `async def` whose body is only `...` (a protocol method, an abstract method, an async stub) gets "INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced invalid code" and the file is not formatted. The same crash happens when an editor's "Format Selection" passes `--line-ranges` covering only the `...` line of an `async def`. For a skipped `def` or `class` header, Black does not crash but gives the `...` a one-space indent. ```console $ printf 'async def f(): # fmt: skip\n ...\n' > skip_async.py $ black --diff -q skip_async.py error: INTERNAL ERROR: Black 26.10.1 on Python (CPython) 3.11.9 produced invalid code: cannot parse: skip_async.py:2:0 ... $ printf 'def f( ): # fmt: skip\n ...\n' > skip_sync.py $ black --diff -q skip_sync.py def f( ): # fmt: skip - ... + ... ``` After this change both files are left as written, and `async def f():\n ...` with `--line-ranges=2-2` is left unchanged instead of crashing. The skipped header, `async` included, becomes a single standalone comment under the `async_stmt` node, and the `funcdef` keeps only its suite. `is_stub_suite` still treated the `...` body as a dummy implementation to join onto the header line, but `visit_funcdef` starts a new line first, so the `...` was emitted at column 0. A suite that no longer follows its colon now is not a stub suite, and the body is emitted as a normal indented block. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before A1["async def f(): # fmt: skip
(STANDALONE_COMMENT)"] --> B1["is_stub_suite: True"] B1 --> C1["visit_funcdef: new line"] C1 --> D1["'...' at column 0: invalid code"] end subgraph After A2["async def f(): # fmt: skip
(STANDALONE_COMMENT)"] --> B2["suite not after ':'
is_stub_suite: False"] B2 --> D2["'...' indented body"] end ``` On the stability policy: the fix only changes output for headers Black was told not to format. The `async` case is a crash. The `def`/`class` case changes a one-space indent that Black itself produced on an otherwise skipped header. With `--line-ranges` selecting only the body line of a sync stub, the unselected header is no longer joined into `def f(): ...`, so lines outside the range stay as written; the new `line_ranges_async_stub_body.py` case covers this. Black 24.1.0 and 25.1.0 fail on both inputs, so this is long-standing rather than a recent regression. Tested on Windows 11, Python 3.11.9: `pytest tests` 752 passed, 14 skipped; `black --check src tests/test_black.py` clean. Both new case files fail on `main` and pass with the change. ### Checklist - did you ... - [ ] Implement any code style changes under the `--preview` style, following the stability policy? - [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary? - [x] Add / update tests if necessary? - [x] Add new / update outdated documentation?

title: Fix blackd startup on Windows with more than 61 logical CPUs
body:
### Description

On Windows with 64 logical CPUs, `blackd` fails during app initialization with `ValueError: max_workers must be <= 61`. The explicit worker count introduced in #5039 bypasses the cap that Python applies to the default process pool on Windows. [ProcessPoolExecutor documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/concurrent.futures.html#concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor)

Share the CLI's existing Windows worker cap with `blackd` so the process pool and request semaphore use the same count. The regression test patches the CPU count before importing `blackd` in a fresh Windows interpreter and calls `make_app()`. It fails on current `main` and passes with the fix.

### Verification

- `tox -e py314` on Windows. 652 passed, 12 skipped in the regular run. All 102 Jupyter tests passed.
- `tox -e run_self` passed. All 49 focused blackd and concurrency tests and mypy on the three changed Python files passed after the final edit.

title: Keep parens around comparison operands with string trailers
body:
### Description

Fixes #3409.

With the unstable `string_processing` feature, this input:

```python
class X:
    def f(self):
        assert remove_color_code(output) == (
            "error: not checking stubs due to mypy build errors:\n{}.pyi:2: "
            'error: Name "f" already defined'.format(TEST_MODULE_NAME)
        )
```

is still reformatted on `main` to the over-long output from the issue:

```python
class X:
    def f(self):
        assert remove_color_code(
            output
        ) == 'error: not checking stubs due to mypy build errors:\n{}.pyi:2: error: Name "f" already defined'.format(
            TEST_MODULE_NAME
        )
```

`StringMerger` joins the two strings, then `StringParenStripper` removes the parentheses. `StringSplitter` only handles a line that starts with the string, optionally after an operator. Here the right-hand split leaves the string after the left operand, so it stays in one piece and the line stays over the limit.

`StringParenStripper` already keeps the parentheses for the same situation after `=`, added for #3497 in #5558. This extends that check to the comparison operators `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=`, so the input above stays as written, when both of these hold:

- The string has a trailer ending in a non-empty bracket, such as `.format(x)` or `% (a, b)`. That bracket is what the right-hand split picks instead of the comparison. Comparisons with a plain string are left alone, and the existing `assert str(suffix_arr) == (...)` cases in `preview_long_strings__regression.py` still pass unchanged.
- The merged string does not fit on a line of its own, using the same width check as `StringParenWrapper`. A string that does fit is still stripped, as in the short cases in the new test.

Like the existing check, this only applies to merged strings (`has_custom_splits`). A single long string in parentheses, or a concatenation with no parentheses around it, is not changed by this PR.

Results, run on Linux with Python 3.13:

- The new case in `preview_long_strings__regression.py` fails on the old `trans.py` and passes with this change.
- `pytest tests --ignore=tests/test_blackd.py`: 619 passed, 3 skipped.
- `black --check`, `isort --check`, `flake8` and `mypy` on `src/black/trans.py` pass, with the versions pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` for `isort`, `flake8` and `mypy`.
- A sweep of 15,840 generated `==` comparisons on the old and new code, through both `--unstable` and `string_processing` alone. It varied string length, argument length, indentation, the left operand (`f()` and `f(output)`), the statement (`assert`, `if`, `return`, assignment, call argument, `and`) and the trailer (`.format(fn(x))`, `.upper()`, `% fn(x)`, `% (first, x)`, none). None failed `assert_equivalent` or `assert_stable` on either side, and no output went from within the line length to over it.

1,952 outputs changed, all with the `.format(fn(x))` or `% (first, x)` trailer:

| Outputs | Change |
|---|---|
| 600 | over the line length before, within it now (all with `f(output)`) |
| 864 | within the line length before and now, but a different shape |
| 488 | over the line length before and now, because the trailer argument itself is too long |

The 864 are a side effect worth a look. When the left operand cannot be split, for example `f()`, the old code already stayed within the limit by splitting at the operator, and this change keeps the parentheses instead:

```python
# before
assert (
    value_of_thing()
    == "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa "
    "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb {}".format(fn(x))
)

# after
assert value_of_thing() == (
    "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa "
    "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb {}".format(fn(x))
)
```

Telling these apart in `StringParenStripper` would mean predicting how the left operand splits, so I left it out. The new test case pins this output. Happy to narrow it if a different shape is preferred here.

title: Fix `# fmt: skip` combined with `# fmt: off` / `# yapf: disable` in the same comment
body:
### Description

A comment that contains both an fmt: off directive and `# fmt: skip`, such as
`# yapf: disable  # fmt: skip` (common when migrating from yapf), is handled
inconsistently. `generate_ignored_nodes()` already treats it as `# fmt: skip`, but
the rest of the conversion still treats it as `# fmt: off`:

1. As a trailing comment, the line is formatted anyway, while `# noqa  # fmt: skip`
   is left alone:

   ```python
   x = [ 1,2 ]  # yapf: disable  # fmt: skip
   ```
   becomes `x = [1, 2]  # yapf: disable  # fmt: skip`.

2. As an own-line comment inside brackets, Black crashes with "produced different
   code on the second pass", because the comment is emitted twice and grows on
   every run:

   ```python
   x = [
       # fmt: off  # fmt: skip
       1,
   ]
   ```

This change lets `# fmt: skip` win consistently, so such a comment behaves the same
as a plain `# fmt: skip`. I found it by inserting fmt comments into the existing
test cases and running Black with its equivalence and stability checks.

title: Fix crash on a commented parenthesized assignment target
body:
### Description

Black crashes with `INTERNAL ERROR: produced different code on the second pass of the formatter` on an assignment whose target is a multi-line parenthesized expression preceded by a standalone comment.

```python
def restore_region(surface, region, sly, slx, sh, sw):
    # The standalone comment is kept.
    (np.frombuffer(surface.get_data(), np.uint32)
     .reshape((sh, sw))[sly, slx]) = region._data
```

The fix lets the target drop its now-invisible parentheses when the only comment is before the opening bracket, and keeps blocking the drop when a comment sits inside the brackets.

#### Root cause

#5606 added this branch to `normalize_invisible_parens`:

```python
elif is_atom_with_invisible_parens(child) and not any(
    "#" in leaf.prefix for leaf in child.leaves()
):
    middle = child.children[1]
    middle.prefix = child.prefix
    child.replace(middle)
```

The guard reads every leaf of the atom, and `child.leaves()` includes the opening bracket. A standalone comment above the statement lives in that bracket's prefix, which is also the atom's prefix, so the guard sees a `#` and refuses to drop the parentheses.

That refusal is what makes the two passes disagree. On the first pass the target keeps its parentheses, so the right-hand side is the part that gets split. On the second pass the target is no longer multi-line, the parentheses are dropped, and the target is split instead. Black compares the two results and aborts.

The comment is not actually at risk. The branch moves `child.prefix` onto the middle node on the next line, so a comment before the opening bracket survives the drop. Only a comment from the opening bracket inward would be lost, and that is what the existing `_atom_has_inner_comments` helper checks, since it looks at `children[1:]`.

#### Verification

Reproduced on unpatched `b4f1fcae`:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=/tmp/black-main/src python -m black -q /tmp/stab2/a.py
error: cannot format /tmp/stab2/a.py: INTERNAL ERROR: Black 26.10.2.dev94+gb1c244db9
on Python (CPython) 3.15.0 produced different code on the second pass of the
formatter. Please report a bug on https://github.com/psf/black/issues.
```

The new fixture case fails on the base commit and passes with the patch:

```
$ pytest tests/test_format.py -q -k remove_parens_from_lhs   # on base, with the new case
1 failed, 1 passed, 313 deselected

$ pytest tests/test_format.py -q -k remove_parens_from_lhs   # with the patch
1 passed
```

Full suite with the patch, `tests/test_blackd.py` excluded because `aiohttp` is not installed in this environment:

```
$ pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/test_blackd.py --ignore=tests/test_rust.py
616 passed, 6 skipped, 31 subtests passed
```

Formatting is stable across repeated passes for the reported case, for blank lines around the comment, and for `# type: ignore`, `# noqa` and `# fmt: skip` in the same position. A comment inside the brackets still keeps the parentheses, as before.

Diff is 40 changed lines across 3 files, against this repository's median of 43.

#### What I did not verify

I did not run the `blackd` test module, which needs the `d` extra. I did not test on Windows or on a compiled (mypyc) build; the reproduction and the suite ran on Linux with CPython 3.15. I did not find a case where `_atom_has_inner_comments` misses a comment, but I only tested placements I could construct by hand.

title: Ensure `parenthesize_expressions_with_comments` is in preview
body:
<!-- Hello! Thanks for submitting a PR. To help make things go a bit smoother
     we would appreciate that you go through this template. -->

### Description

<!-- Good things to put here include: reasoning for the change (please link
     any relevant issues!), any noteworthy (or hacky) choices to be aware of,
     or what the problem resolved here looked like ... we won't mind a ranty
     story :) -->

Not only was #5638 supposed to be implemented in preview itself, it also seems to trigger the `parenthesize_expressions_with_comments` fix in stable style. It's now gated.

### Checklist - did you ...

<!-- If any of the following items aren't relevant for your contribution,
     please still tick them so we know you've gone through the checklist.

     - Please familiarize yourself with Black's stability policy, linked
       below. Code style changes are only allowed under the `--preview` flag
       until maintainers move them to stable in the next calendar year.
     - All user-facing changes should get a changelog entry. If this isn't
       user-facing, signal to us that this should get the magical label to
       silence the check.
     - Tests are required for all bugfixes and new features.

title: Fix --line-ranges not removing selected trailing blank lines
body:
## Why

`--line-ranges` never removes the extra blank lines at the end of a file, even when the range reaches the last line. A plain run does:

```console
$ printf 'x  =  1\n\n' > t.py
$ black --line-ranges=1-2 t.py
reformatted t.py
$ od -c t.py | tail -2
0000000   x       =       1  \n  \n
$ black --check t.py; echo $?
would reformat t.py
1
```

and the second `--line-ranges` run reports the file as unchanged, so incremental formatting can never make it pass `--check`. The same file with `black t.py` (no range) becomes `x = 1\n`.

## Cause

`format_str` runs two passes. After the first one it narrows the ranges to follow the code that is left:

```python
lines = adjusted_lines(lines, src_contents, dst_contents)
```

When the first pass drops the trailing blank lines, `adjusted_lines([(1, 2)], "x  =  1\n\n", "x = 1\n")` returns `[(1, 1)]` — the code that was on line 1 is one line long now. The final guard, `_restore_unselected_trailing_blank_lines`, compares the *narrowed* ranges against the dropped lines:

```python
if all(
    not line.strip()
    and not any(start <= line_number <= end for start, end in lines)
    ...
```

Line 2 is no longer inside `[(1, 1)]`, so the blank line is treated as an unselected line and appended back. The guard is doing what it was written for (#5613, #5634): blank lines the caller did not ask about must survive. It is only being handed the wrong ranges.

## What changed

`format_str` keeps the sanitized ranges separately (`requested_lines`) and passes those to the restore guard. The narrowed ranges are still what the second pass formats. Nothing else changes: a range that stops before the last line still preserves the trailing blank lines, which is covered by the second assertion in the new test.

## Test

`tests/test_black.py::BlackTestCase::test_line_ranges_remove_selected_trailing_blank_lines`

- Before: `AssertionError: assert 'x = 1\n\n' == 'x = 1\n'`.
- After: `17 passed` for `-k line_ranges`, `649 passed, 14 skipped` for the whole suite.
- Mutation: putting the narrowed `lines` back into the guard (leaving the rest of the change in place) fails the new test again, so the test pins the actual cause rather than the symptom.

## Checklist

- [x] Not a style change — no `--preview` gate is involved.
- [x] `CHANGES.md` entry, under "Stable style", next to #5634 which is the same code path.
- [x] Tests added.
- [x] No documentation change needed; the documented behaviour ("try its best to only format these lines") is unchanged, and a selected range now matches a full-file run.

## AI assistance

**Tool(s) used:** WorkBuddy (Claude-based AI coding agent)

**How you used it:** It found the divergence while running `--line-ranges` over a real package corpus, traced it to `adjusted_lines` narrowing the range before the trailing-blank-line guard, wrote the fix and the regression test, and ran the before/after, mutation, full-suite and lint checks. I reviewed the diff and take responsibility for it.

- [x] I've read and understand every line of this change.

title: Fix crash on `# fmt: off` in an f-string with `=` or a t-string
body:
### Description

An indented `# fmt: off` in the expression of an f-string field with `=` crashes Black:

```python
x = f"{a
    # fmt: off
=}"
```

fails with "INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced code that is not equivalent to the source". With `=`, Python keeps the source of the expression in the string, without the comments but with the whitespace around them, so this string starts with `"a\n    \n="`. Black turns the `# fmt: off` region into a STANDALONE_COMMENT and, like everywhere else, drops the indentation of the `# fmt: off` line and the whitespace on blank lines before it. The f-string is then written out as it is in the tree, so the comment ends up in column 0 and the string changes. The same happens after the `=` (`f"{a=` ... `# fmt: off` ... `!r}"`), inside brackets in the expression, and in every t-string field, because a t-string keeps the source of each expression in its `Interpolation`, with or without `=`. 26.10.1 crashes on these too.

Where Python keeps that text, the STANDALONE_COMMENT now gets the whole prefix before the `# fmt: off` comment, so the whitespace stays as written. That's the expression of a t-string field, or of an f-string field with `=`, up to the `!` or `:` of the field. Fields in a format spec only count with their own `=`, since a t-string doesn't keep the source there.

This only changes code that crashed before, so it's in the stable style. In other f-string fields the comment still moves to column 0, which doesn't change the string, so I left that as is.

I generated variants of a `# fmt: off` in f-string and t-string fields: 20 field shapes (with and without `=`, before and after the `=`, before `!r` and format specs, in brackets, in a nested f-string and in a format spec), 17 placements and indentations of `# fmt: off`, `# fmt: on`, `# fmt: skip` and comments, 4 string prefixes and quotes, and 8 statement contexts. Over 97,920 runs on Python 3.14 in stable, preview and unstable, with line lengths 88, 30 and 1, 33,390 crashes on `main` are fixed, no other output changes and nothing new crashes. Formatting `main`'s output again with this branch changes nothing. The runs that still crash are two separate cases: a comment-only `# fmt: off` ... `# fmt: on` block in a field loses the newline after `# fmt: on`, with or without `=` (`f"{a` ... `# fmt: off` ... `# fmt: on` ... `+ b}"`), and a nested f-string in a field with `=` that has trailing whitespace after a `# fmt: off` in column 0, since Python also keeps the comments of the nested f-string. A mutation fuzz that adds the same comments to the f-string and t-string fields of the test cases (20,000 samples) gives the same result: 1,327 crashes fixed and the same output everywhere else.

title: Skip notebook cells that can't be tokenized instead of failing the whole notebook
body:
### Description

One notebook cell that the tokenizer rejects makes the whole notebook fail to format. With these two cells:

```python
import os
files=os.listdir( '.' )
```

```
!find . -name "*.pyc" -exec rm {} \;
```

`black --check --diff nb.ipynb` prints `error: cannot format nb.ipynb: ('unexpected character after line continuation character', (1, 37))` and exits with 123, so the first cell isn't formatted either (3.11 says `('EOF in multi-line statement', (2, 0))`). The same happens on 3.12+ for Windows paths in magics (`%cd C:\Users\me`, `!dir C:\Users`) and an apostrophe in a shell command (`!echo don't panic`), and on every version for a cell that is still being written, like `x = (1,`. It reproduces with 26.10.1 too. The docs list "Invalid syntax" under "Cells that Black will skip", but here such a cell fails the whole file, for example in the `black-jupyter` pre-commit hook.

`format_cell()` tokenizes the cell in `remove_trailing_semicolon()` before the `except SyntaxError` that skips invalid cells, so the `tokenize.TokenError` got through. This moves that call into the `try` and catches `TokenError` as well. On 3.11 the `;` in `\;` is taken for a trailing semicolon and the cell can't be tokenized without it, so putting it back gets the same guard. These cells are now left unchanged and the rest of the notebook is formatted.

Ran: `pytest tests/test_ipynb.py --run-optional jupyter -m jupyter` on CPython 3.14, 3.12, 3.11 and PyPy 3.11 (102 passed; on main the new test fails 6/6 on 3.12+ and 4/6 on 3.11 and PyPy).
Ran: `pytest tests --run-optional no_jupyter` and `pytest tests --run-optional jupyter -m jupyter` on 3.14 and 3.11.
Checked: `black --check .`, and isort, flake8 and prettier through pre-commit.

title: Fix crash on `# fmt: off` before the trailing comma in brackets
body:
### Description

A `# fmt: off` between the last item in brackets and its trailing comma crashes Black:

```python
x = [
    a,
    b
    # fmt: off
    ,
]
```

fails with "INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced invalid code" because the output has a second comma after `b`. The same happens in calls, subscripts, dicts, `from` imports and `def` parameters (there even with a single item), with a `# fmt: on` or a comment after the comma, and when the region holds the rest of the last item instead of the comma, like `+ 1`, `.c(d)` or `= 1` in a `def`. With `+ 1` the output parses but means something else (`[a, b, +1]`), so Black reports "produced code that is not equivalent to the source". 26.10.1 crashes on all of these, and the list and call cases have crashed since 24.1.0.

The region becomes a STANDALONE_COMMENT, and the trailing comma logic treats it like any other standalone comment. `delimiter_split` adds the trailing comma after the last leaf that isn't a STANDALONE_COMMENT, so that it goes before comments at the end of the brackets (#3393), and `bracket_split_build_line` does the same for imports and `def` parameters. Here that leaf is `b`, and the comma or the rest of the item comes after it, hidden. Both now stop at code hidden by `# fmt: off`, `# fmt: skip` or `--line-ranges` (a STANDALONE_COMMENT with `fmt_pass_converted_first_leaf` set), so no comma is added before it. None is added after it either, since it may already end in one. `delimiter_split` already worked that way when the hidden code was the last leaf.

This only changes code that crashed before, so it's in the stable style. I generated variants of the last item in brackets: 24 contexts (assignments, calls, subscripts, `return`, `assert`, `del`, `for`, decorators, `from` imports, `def` and class headers, type parameters, dicts, nested brackets), several item shapes, and 27 placements of `# fmt: off`, `# fmt: on`, `# fmt: skip` and comments around the last item and its comma. Over 20,040 runs in stable, preview and unstable, with line lengths 88, 30 and 1, and with `--skip-magic-trailing-comma`, 7,700 crashes on `main` are fixed, no other output changes and nothing new crashes. The 81 runs that still crash are the `--unstable` problem with `x = [(` ... `)]` and the unclosed `# fmt: off` before a single item that is only fixed in preview, both from #5643. A mutation fuzz over the test cases (adding `# fmt: off` before trailing commas and in the middle of lines, comments, `# fmt: skip` and `--line-ranges`, 15,963 samples) gives the same result: 2,172 crashes fixed and the same output everywhere else.

title: Fix line numbers in parse errors and --line-ranges when the file starts with blank lines
body:
## Description

`_format_str_once()` parsed `normalized_contents.lstrip()` instead of the source as-is. Stripping the leading whitespace shifts every line number in the parse tree down by the number of stripped lines, which breaks two user-visible line-number consumers when a file starts with blank lines (or other whitespace-carrying lines):

1. **Parse errors report the wrong location.** For a file whose syntax error is on line 4:

   ```
   $ printf '\n\n\ndef f(:\n    pass\n' > leading.py
   $ black leading.py
   error: cannot parse: leading.py:1:6      <- wrong, the error is on line 4
   ```

   This regressed the `file:line:column` parse-error reporting introduced in #5237 for any file that starts with blank lines.

2. **`--line-ranges` selects the wrong lines.** The first formatting pass compares user-supplied (original-file) line numbers against tree linenos. With 3 leading blank lines, `--line-ranges 5-5` actually selects tree line 5, which is the file's line 8:

   ```python
   # source (real lines: blank, blank, blank, a=4, b=5, c=6, d=7, e=8, f=9)
   $ black --line-ranges 5-5 file.py   # expects only "b" to be formatted
   # before: both "b" AND "e" got reformatted
   # after:  only "b" is reformatted
   ```

   Depending on the file, the shifted selection can also miss the requested line entirely (the range intersects no statement, nothing is selected, and the file is reported as unchanged). The diff-based mapping in the second pass (`adjusted_lines`) usually re-heals multi-pass runs, which is why this has gone unnoticed — but the wrong line that the *first* pass reformats survives into the final output, as the second test demonstrates.

## Fix

Parse the source as-is. blib2to3 handles leading whitespace correctly (it reports proper linenos for leading blank lines, NBSP, form feeds, etc.), and `EmptyLineTracker._maybe_empty_lines()` already drops blank lines before the first line of the file, so the formatted output is unchanged for normal files — only the line numbers become correct.

## Test-suite note

`test_line_ranges_removed_at_start_of_file_stay_unformatted` still passes: black intentionally removes leading blank lines at the file head, and that behavior is unchanged. Only the *numbering* is fixed.

## Testing

- Added `test_invalid_input_error_line_number_with_leading_blank_lines`: parse error in a file with 3 leading blank lines must be reported at `4:6`, not `1:6`. Fails on main (got `1:6`), passes with this PR.
- Added `test_line_ranges_after_leading_blank_lines_target_the_right_lines`: `lines=[(5, 5)]` on a file with 3 leading blank lines must format only line 5. Fails on main (line 8 was also reformatted), passes with this PR.
- Full suite (`pytest tests --run-optional no_jupyter`): 645 passed, 2 failed before and after — the 2 failures are environment artifacts of running on a machine with the `jupyter` extra installed (`test_no_ipynb` asserts those deps are absent), unrelated to this change.

title: Keep the blank line after a nested import that is followed by a comment
body:
### Description

Since #5493, a comment right after an import inside a function, class, `try` or `if` block no longer gets a blank line after the import. 26.10.1 and earlier add it, and module-level imports still get it:

```python
def f():
    import json
    # comment
    return json
```

`black --check` passes on this with main but fails with 26.10.1, so code formatted by the next release would be reformatted again by 26.10.1. A common case is `try: import termios` followed by an explanatory comment.

The comment exclusion from #5493 was meant for imports outside `--line-ranges` ("excluding unselected standalone comments and pairs of unselected lines"), but it also applied after real imports. This moves it into the branch for imports converted by `--line-ranges`. There, `not current_line.is_comment` also covers converted lines, since those are standalone comments, so the separate check for two converted lines is no longer needed.

I found this by formatting CPython's `Lib` and a few packages (about 2,700 files) with 26.10.1 and with main: 32 files differ only by this blank line, and with this change they match 26.10.1 again. diff-shades likely won't show it, because its projects are already formatted and existing blank lines are kept.

The #5493 changelog entry (and #5502's) ended up under 26.10.1, so I added this PR's number to it there. Happy to move it or drop it for `ci: skip news`.

Ran: `pytest tests` (the new case in `import_line_collapse.py` fails without the change) and `tox -e run_self`.
Checked: every single-line `--line-ranges` selection on import/comment/statement samples. Output only changes when the import line itself is selected, and then matches 26.10.1; #5493's tests still pass.

title: Fix `# fmt: skip` on the last line of a multi-line conditional expression in brackets
body:
### Description

When a conditional expression inside brackets spans several lines and `# fmt: skip` is on its last line, Black produces invalid code:

```python
x = (
    a
    if c else d,  # fmt: skip
    e,
)
```

```
error: cannot format repro.py: INTERNAL ERROR: ... produced invalid code: cannot parse: 5:6:         ) e,
```

With `--fast` it's written out silently; a variant like `a  # comment` / `+ b if c else d,  # fmt: skip` / `(e),` turns the tuple into a call: `(a ... else d,  # fmt: skip\n)(e)`.

`# fmt: skip` hides only the code on its own line (`if c else d,`), so that hidden code ends the `test` node and also takes the comma after it. `visit_test` then wraps the node in invisible parentheses and the closing one lands after the comma. #5464 fixed the case where the whole ternary is on the skipped line; this is the multi-line one.

`visit_test` now skips the invisible parentheses when the node's last leaf is code hidden by `# fmt: skip`, like the existing check for hidden code at the start. Three multi-line cases added to `fmtskip_conditional_in_brackets.py`; they fail on `main` and pass with the change.

The same thing still happens under `--preview` for a dict value via `wrap_long_dict_values_in_parens`; I left that alone since #5627 is reworking that code.

title: Remove redundant parentheses around yields of tuples
body:
### Description

Fixes #1553.

With `--preview`, `parenthesize_tuple_in_yield` (#5170) gives a yielded tuple its own parentheses, but the parentheses around the `yield` itself, as in `(yield a, b)` or `x = (yield a, b)`, are still kept because of the comma. This removes them in the same places as for other yields (expression statements and the right-hand side of plain and augmented assignments), so these lines are formatted as if written without them.

On `main`, they only go away on Black's internal second pass, and only if the first pass made the tuple's parentheses visible, for example by splitting it one element per line as in the issue's example. A line like `(yield a, b)` keeps them.

This is part of `parenthesize_tuple_in_yield` rather than a new feature because it relies on the tuple's parentheses: without them, a long `x = yield a, b` is split the misleading way the issue describes.

title: Fix blackd client encoding for custom Content-Type charsets
body:
### Description

BlackDClient always encodes requests as UTF-8, even when a custom Content-Type declares another charset. The server follows that header: formatting `message='café'` with Latin-1 or Windows-1252 silently changes the literal to `cafÃ©`; UTF-16 instead fails to decode.

Use aiohttp's StringPayload to encode the source consistently with the declared Content-Type, retaining the UTF-8 default. The regression test makes actual HTTP requests for five content types, each with formatted and unformatted input, covering both 200 and 204 responses.

Validation on Python 3.12 / Windows:
- The identical new test has four failing subtests on the base client and all ten passing with the fix.
- Main test phase: 645 passed, 7 skipped, 42 subtests passed.
- blackd tests with minimum aiohttp 3.10.0: 41 passed, 10 subtests passed (also tested with 3.14.5).
- tox run_self passed (68 files unchanged). Import-order, lint, end-of-file and whitespace hooks passed.

title: Fix crashes on a `# fmt: off` region that ends at a closing bracket
body:
### Description

This fixes two crashes with a `# fmt: off` region that ends at the closing bracket.

**`# fmt: off` without `# fmt: on` before a single item.** Without a `# fmt: on`, the region runs to the end of the brackets (#4363, #5585), but Black crashes when the brackets hold a single name, number or string:

```python
x = [
    # fmt: off
    1
]
```

fails with "Unable to match a closing bracket to the following opening bracket", also with a `# fmt: on` after the `]`. `x = f(` ... `)`, `assert (` ... `), "message"` and similar fail with "INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced invalid code", and `from a import (` ... `)` fails with a bare `AssertionError`. 26.10.1 and 23.1.0 crash on these too.

`generate_ignored_nodes` takes the first ignored node and then its next siblings, until it finds `# fmt: on` or runs out of siblings. For `a + b` or `a, b` that walk stays inside the node between the brackets. A lone leaf, though, is a direct child of the atom or trailer, so its next sibling is the closing bracket, and the bracket gets hidden along with whatever follows it in the same node. The walk now stops at a closing bracket unless the region also took its opening bracket (like the whole `[1,  2]` in `foo(` ... `# fmt: off` ... `[1,  2])`).

Where this didn't crash, the output was wrong anyway. `print(` ... `# fmt: off` ... `a` ... `)` moved `# fmt: off` to column 0, and in `class A(` ... `# fmt: off` ... `B` ... `):` the region also took the `):` and the class body, which was left unformatted. Type parameters are also direct children of their brackets, so `def f[` ... `# fmt: off` ... `T,  B,` ... `](a,):` had the same problem however many there were. Now `# fmt: off` stays indented, as it already does with two items in a call, and the code after the closing bracket is formatted. Code like this that was already formatted by Black will change, but only with an unclosed `# fmt: off` in one of these brackets, so this part is behind the `end_fmt_off_at_closing_bracket` preview feature. In the stable style these cases behave as on `main` until the feature is promoted. The cases that still crash in stable are tested in `tests/data/miscellaneous/` with a preview-only test, since the `tests/data/cases` harness also formats each case in the other style.

**`# fmt: skip` on the closing bracket.** This fix is in the stable style, since it only changes code that crashed before. Once the region ends at the closing bracket, a lone item behaves like two items, and with two items this already crashes on `main` and 26.10.1:

```python
x = [
    # fmt: off
    a,  b  # comment
]  # fmt: skip
```

fails with "INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced different code on the second pass". The same happens with a `# comment` line before the `]`, or a comment before `# fmt: on`. The comments that end the region are part of it (#5585), but the newline after them stays in the prefix of the `]`. When `# fmt: skip` hides the statement, `_handle_regular_fmt_block` adds a newline after hidden code whose last line has a comment, because for `B,  # fmt: skip` that newline was taken from the prefix of the next leaf. Here it wasn't, so every pass adds a blank line before the `]`. For a `# fmt: off` region, that newline (and the joining of the last comment line from #5401) is now left out when the prefix of the next leaf starts with one. Code hidden by `# fmt: skip` and comment-only `# fmt: off` blocks take the newline after their last comment, so there a newline at the start of that prefix is a blank line, and they keep the current behavior. This also covers a region that is directly in the hidden code, like `class C(` ... `# fmt: off` ... `B` ... `):  # fmt: skip`, where the `"\n" in next_node.prefix` check added a blank line before the `)`.

In the output of `fmtskip_after_fmtoff_in_brackets.py`, the `# fmt: off` lines end up in column 0. `# fmt: skip` on the closing bracket already does that to a `# fmt: off` inside the brackets on `main` (with `a,  b` and no comment), so I left it alone.

I generated variants of a `# fmt: off` inside brackets: 35 contexts (assignments, calls, subscripts, annotations, `assert`, `del`, `return`/`yield`, operands, `from` imports, class/def headers, `with`/`if`/`for`/`while` headers, decorators, nested brackets), 17 item shapes, and 10 placements of `# fmt: off`, `# fmt: on` and comments, at module level, in a function and followed by another statement.

- Without `# fmt: skip` (78,438 runs in stable, preview and unstable, and with line lengths 88, 30 and 1): 9,468 crashes on `main` are fixed. The 2,790 outputs that differ are all the unclosed `# fmt: off` described above, and running this branch on `main`'s output changes nothing else. The 114 runs that still crash are an existing `--unstable` problem with `x = [(` ... `)]` that also happens with a `# fmt: on`.
- With `# fmt: skip` added on the opening, item or closing line (147,123 runs): 37,137 crashes on `main` are fixed, and none are left. The 2,202 outputs that differ are again lone items.
- A random mutation fuzz over the test cases (adding `# fmt: off`, `# fmt: on`, `# fmt: skip`, comments and `--line-ranges`), 2 × 25,000 samples on `main` and on this branch: 509 crashes fixed. The 340 outputs that differ are lone items and type parameters as above, the blank lines from the second crash removed, or a lone item now formatted like two items. One sample crashes that didn't before: a type parameter list with `# fmt: off` right before its trailing comma, after a commented item (`def f[` ... `U  # c` ... `# fmt: off` ... `,` ... `]`). On `main`, the same thing in a list or call already crashes (`x = [` ... `T,` ... `U` ... `# fmt: off` ... `,` ... `]` gets a second comma), so that's a separate bug.

body:

title: cache: treat an unreadable cache file as a miss
body:
### Description

Black treats the cache as an optimization everywhere except one place: `Cache.read()` opens the pickle outside the `try` that handles a malformed cache. If that `open()` raises `OSError`, it escapes into `reformat_one()`, which reports the **source file** as failed:

```
$ BLACK_CACHE_DIR=... black x.py
error: cannot format .../x.py: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '.../cache.-.88.1.0.0.0.1.0.0.c3641f85.pickle'

Oh no! 1 file failed to reformat.
exit=123
```

On Windows this is not hypothetical: two Black processes sharing a cache directory are enough. One calls `os.replace()` (which `Cache.write()` already does), the other calls `open("rb")` on the same path at that moment, and the reader gets `PermissionError: [Errno 13]` — a sharing violation. That is what has been reddening `main`:

| run | job | failing test |
|---|---|---|
| [40977901760](https://github.com/psf/black/actions/runs/40977901760) | 3.14, windows-11-arm | `test_cache_isnt_written_if_no_jupyter_deps_dir` |
| [40609983148](https://github.com/psf/black/actions/runs/40609983148) | 3.14, windows-11-arm | `test_cache_isnt_written_if_no_jupyter_deps_dir` |
| [40438903941](https://github.com/psf/black/actions/runs/40438903941) | 3.10, windows-latest | `test_ipynb_diff_with_no_change` |
| [40259878945](https://github.com/psf/black/actions/runs/40259878945) | 3.15, windows-11-arm | `test_cache_isnt_written_if_no_jupyter_deps_single` |

All four logs contain `Permission denied: 'C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local\black\black\Cache\<version>\cache.-.88.1.0.0.0.1.0.0.<hash>.pickle'`, on four different tests — so the test is not the cause; the shared cache read is.

### Fix

Move `open()` inside the handler that already tolerates a corrupt cache, and catch `OSError` (of which `PermissionError` is a subclass). An unreadable cache is a cache miss; the next `Cache.write()`, which already ignores `OSError`, replaces the file. Formatting results are unchanged.

### Tests

New `TestCaching::test_cache_unreadable_file_is_a_miss` makes the cache path unopenable, asserts `Cache.read()` returns an empty cache, and that the CLI still reformats the file:

- before the fix: `1 failed` — `IsADirectoryError` out of `Cache.read()`
- after the fix: `1 passed`
- `tests/test_black.py tests/test_ipynb.py`: 309 passed; the 9 failures are the same 9 on the unmodified base in this environment (color/TTY/CRLF, unrelated)
- `black --check src/black/cache.py tests/test_black.py`: clean

The `CHANGES.md` entry is in the second commit, since it needs the PR number.

Note: #5579 also edits this method (it swaps `pickle.load` for `safe_pickle.load` inside the same `try`). The two changes are orthogonal — whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase and no behavior decision.

### Checklist

- [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary? (follow-up commit)
- [x] Add / update tests if necessary?
- [ ] Add new / update outdated documentation? (not applicable)

title: Keep optional parens for commented assignment RHS
body:
Fixes #3925.

### Problem

For the input from #3925, Black's stable style currently produces a 93-character first line (over the 88-character default):

```python
abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdefghijklmnopqr = abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcd | (
```

That output is not a fixed point: running Black again on it produces a different result.

### Cause

`_prefer_split_rhs_oop_over_rhs()` in `src/black/linegen.py` prefers the split that omits optional parentheses whenever the assignment target has no brackets, without checking the width of the resulting head. When the RHS contains standalone comments, the split body has to stay on separate lines and cannot rejoin the head, so the overlong head becomes the final first line.

### Fix

Keep the optional parentheses when all of these hold:

- the omitted-paren head is over the line length;
- the head with parentheses fits;
- the RHS body has standalone comments;
- the omitted-paren head has no closing bracket (there is no earlier split point for the splitter to try);
- the omitted-paren head has no comments (the overflow is not comment-driven).

This drops the operator and parenthesis-specific conditions from the earlier revision.

No preview gate: the old output is not idempotent, and the change leaves every existing test expectation and every stable diff-shades result untouched.

### Tests

- New `tests/data/cases/overlong_commented_rhs.py` uses the exact issue snippet: the first line goes from 93 to 60 characters, and the longest line is 84.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_format.py -q`: 306 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/ -q`: 644 passed, 3 skipped, 31 subtests. The 2 color-output failures also fail on unmodified `main` in this environment.
- `python -m mypy src/black/linegen.py` and `python -m black --check src/`: clean.
- diff-shades: no changes for either `--stable` or `--preview` across all 22 projects (3.15M lines).

title: Fix --line-ranges crash on clauses with their body on the same line
body:
### Description

With `--line-ranges`, Black fails on a file when a statement outside the selected lines is an `if`, `for`, `while` or `try` statement with more than one clause and one of the clauses has its body on the same line. Editors use `--line-ranges` for "Format Selection" and for formatting only the modified lines, so this shows up in older code that uses one-line clauses. For example, `black --line-ranges=12-12 --diff example.py` on:

```python
class Dialog:
    def ask(self):
        if self.saved:
            reply = "yes"
        else: reply = "no"
        return reply

def check(path):
    try: f = open(path)
    except OSError:
        return None
    return  f
```

fails with "INTERNAL ERROR: Black ... produced invalid code: cannot parse" and exits with 123. CPython's `Lib/idlelib/iomenu.py` fails the same way with `--line-ranges=216-230`. In other cases Black doesn't crash but changes lines outside the ranges, e.g. `if sizeof(kind) == 2: c_uint16 = kind` in `ctypes/__init__.py` becomes `if sizeof(kind) == 2:c_uint16 = kind`.

A body on the same line as its clause was handled as a line of its own. The top-level pass converted it to a standalone comment without its newline, so the next clause was joined to it (`if a: b()else:`), and the line-by-line pass converted it once on its own and again with the next clause's header. A last clause such as `else: c()` after an indented block converted the whole statement after its inner lines were already converted, which lost their indentation. Now such a body is converted together with its clause, so each clause line becomes one standalone comment. One-liners with a single clause, such as `def f(): ...`, keep the existing path. For an `async for` or `async with` statement, the `async` keyword is now joined only to its first clause line, so a later `else:` line isn't converted together with it. With the change, the example above only changes `return  f` to `return f`.

Ran: `pytest tests --run-optional no_jupyter`, then the jupyter tests with the extra installed, `black --check .`, and isort, flake8, mypy and prettier at the pre-commit versions (no new findings).
Checked: every one-line and three-line range of about 40 small variants (comments between clauses, `# fmt: skip` and `# fmt: off`, `# type: ignore`, multi-line headers and bodies, backslashes, semicolons, CRLF, tabs, `match`, `except*`, decorated and async one-liners, `async for` with `else`, pyi and preview): 186 errors on `main`, none with the patch, and no range where the patch changes a line that `main` kept. On the CPython 3.14 stdlib with single-line clause bodies moved onto their clause line, 902 of 2,220 random ranges failed on `main` and none with the patch, and all of them pass the equivalence and stability checks. On the unmodified stdlib, 3 of 3,624 ranges failed on `main` and none with the patch; the 4 other differences are unselected lines that are now kept as they were.

title: Preserve trailing blank lines at EOF in unclosed fmt: off blocks (#496)
body:
### Description

Fixes #496. Supersedes stale PR #5336 and addresses maintainer review feedback from @cobaltt7.

#### Problem
In `lib2to3`, blank lines and comments at the very end of a file attach to `ENDMARKER.prefix` or terminal `DEDENT` leaves rather than to preceding statement nodes. When a `# fmt: off` block reaches EOF without a matching `# fmt: on`, `ignored_nodes` in `_handle_regular_fmt_block` only contained statement nodes, discarding any trailing blank lines on terminal dedents and the endmarker.

#### Solution
- Added `_get_endmarker_and_dedents()` in `src/black/comments.py` to traverse from `ignored_nodes[-1]` to `ENDMARKER`, collecting all intervening `DEDENT` leaves across arbitrary nesting levels.
- If no `# fmt: on` follows on any of these EOF nodes, their prefixes (including trailing comments and blank lines) are preserved in the standalone comment's hidden value and cleared from the EOF nodes.
- If `# fmt: on` is present, EOF blank lines continue to be normalized as expected.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/test_black.py` covering top-level, indented, nested, LF/CRLF, and comment scenarios.
- Added changelog entry in the **Stable style** section of `CHANGES.md`.

### Checklist - did you ...

- [x] Implement any code style changes under the `--preview` style, following the stability policy? *(N/A - bug fix in stable style for # fmt: off)*
- [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary?

title: Fix crash on fmt: skip after the last base of a skipped class header
body:
### Description

A class header with `# fmt: skip` crashes when its last base or keyword argument also has a `# fmt: skip`:

```python
class A(
    B,  # fmt: skip
):  # fmt: skip
    pass
```

```console
$ black repro.py
error: INTERNAL ERROR: Black 9a1f64e on Python (CPython) 3.12.15 produced invalid code:
cannot parse: repro.py:3:4
        pass
       ^
ParseError: bad input
```

The output it can't parse has the header's `):` inside the comment:

```python
class A(
    B,  # fmt: skip):  # fmt: skip
    pass
```

The same happens in these cases:
- `B` without the comma, or more than one base with the `# fmt: skip` on the last one;
- `metaclass=M`;
- a decorated class, or a nested class.

26.10.1 crashes the same way. `def`, `if`, `while`, `for` and `with` headers with the same two comments format fine.

What happens:
- The inner `# fmt: skip` hides `B,`. It takes its comment, together with the newline after it, from the prefix of the header's `)`.
- The header's `# fmt: skip` then turns the whole header into one standalone comment, and the hidden `B,  # fmt: skip` needs that newline back.
- For `def` and the other statements, the brackets sit inside a node (`parameters`, `atom`), so the hidden part goes through `stringify_node`. That adds a newline after a standalone comment whose last line has a `#` (#5597).
- A class's parentheses are direct children of `classdef`, so the hidden base went through `stringify_standalone_comment` instead. That only added the newline when the next leaf's prefix had one, and here the prefix had lost it.

`stringify_standalone_comment` now also adds the newline when the last line has a `#`, as `stringify_node` does. The header is then kept exactly as written.

To check that nothing else changes:
- I generated 1,079 inputs and formatted each in stable and preview mode (2,158 runs). They are compound statement headers (class, def, if, while, for, with, except) and statements, with `# fmt: skip`, `# fmt:skip`, `# type: ignore` or another comment on one line, and `# fmt: skip` on two or three lines.
  - Main crashes on 56 of the runs and this branch on 10.
  - Every run that main formats gives the same output on this branch.
  - The 10 that still crash are a decorator ending in `)  # fmt: skip` right before `class A(  # fmt: skip`. That is unstable formatting ("produced different code on the second pass") on main and on 26.10.1 too, and this change doesn't fix it.
- The 12 files in a Python 3.12 install (stdlib and site-packages) that contain `fmt: skip` or `fmt: off` format to identical output on main and on this branch.

### Checklist - did you ...

- [x] Implement any code style changes under the `--preview` style, following the stability policy? (A crash fix, so stable as the policy allows; code that formatted before formats the same.)
- [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary?
- [x] Add / update tests if necessary? (New case `fmtskip_class_header_base.py`: the cases above and a nested class with a docstring. It fails on main with the crash.)
- [x] Add new / update outdated documentation? (Not needed.)

Test results:
- `pytest tests`: 725 passed. The only failures are `test_expression_diff_with_color` and `test_piping_diff_with_color`, which fail the same way on main in my terminal (no ANSI codes in the output).
- `pytest tests --run-optional jupyter -m jupyter`: 89 passed.
- `black --check .` (run_self) and the pre-commit hooks (isort, flake8, mypy, prettier, end-of-file, trailing whitespace) pass.

title: Fix unstable formatting of multi-line comparison operand parentheses
body:
### Description

With `--preview`, this test from haystack (formatted by another tool, which wraps a long comparison operand in parentheses) fails:

```python
def test_offloadable_content_blocks(self, tmp_path, result, expected):
    assert _offloadable_content_blocks(result=tool_result, store=FileSystemToolResultStore(root=tmp_path)) == (
        expected
    )
```

```
error: cannot format x.py: INTERNAL ERROR: Black ... produced different code on the second pass of the formatter.
```

It comes from `remove_redundant_comparison_parentheses` (#5539) alone. The feature keeps the parentheses of an operand that spans several lines (`_is_atom_multiline`). Black then joins them into `== (expected)` on the first pass, and on the second pass, they aren't multiline any more, so they are removed. But they are only made invisible, and the invisible parens at the end of the line let the right hand split omit them, so the line is split as

```python
    assert _offloadable_content_blocks(
        result=tool_result, store=FileSystemToolResultStore(root=tmp_path)
    ) == expected
```

while the same code written without parentheses (`== expected`, which the next run sees) is split as

```python
    assert (
        _offloadable_content_blocks(
            result=tool_result, store=FileSystemToolResultStore(root=tmp_path)
        )
        == expected
    )
```

When the parentheses are removed on the first pass, Black's second pass works from the text without them, so this only shows when the removal is delayed by the multiline check. It affects any right operand that doesn't end in a bracket (a name, attribute, string, number, `-x`, subscript, `await`, `None`) in `assert`, `if` and assignments: 78 of the combinations I tried were unstable on `main`.

`_normalize_comparison_operands` now drops the invisible parens after making them invisible, the same way `normalize_invisible_parens` already does for assignment targets ("Drop the now invisible parens so the target splits the same way as one written without parentheses") and the generator-argument code does for generators. Operands with comments keep them, as there. The output is then the one Black gives for the operand written without parentheses. Operands that stay multiline, such as long strings and the existing "Multiline operands" cases, keep their parentheses as before.

I found this by formatting 14,029 files (CPython stdlib and a few projects) with `--preview`: this haystack file was the only failure. With this change, it is the only one of the 14,029 whose `--preview` output changes, and none fail.

The one diff-shades change (warehouse, `OrganizationApplication.status == (OrganizationApplicationStatus.Submitted)` in a split call) is the same thing with parentheses on one line: the invisible parens were used to split the operand, as `== (` ... `)`, and now it is split as Black splits `== OrganizationApplicationStatus.Submitted` written without them (I checked the output is identical, and stable).

### Checklist - did you ...

- [x] Implement any code style changes under the `--preview` style, following the stability policy? (Only the `remove_redundant_comparison_parentheses` preview feature changes.)
- [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary?
